operationalSituations.description: Developer runs cfusa check/lint in CI or as a pre-commit gate as the sole safety-relevant static analysis step for a change
Developer runs cfusa impact locally against a git repository, passing --from/--to ref arguments that may originate from an untrusted source (e.g. a CI job templated from a pull request)
cfusa release/qualify artifacts (SBOM, provenance, qualification record) are generated and submitted as evidence into an external safety case or certification package
Developer manually computes an ASIL rating via cfusa hara asil from S/E/C parameters during hazard analysis

hazards.description: Tool reports no violations on a file that contains real safety violations (false-negative), leading the developer to believe code is safe when it is not
Tool reports excessive false-positives, causing the developer to disable checks or ignore findings, masking real violations
Command injection via unsanitised --from/--to git refs passed to popen(), allowing arbitrary shell execution on the developer's machine
SBOM or qualification record is generated with incorrect checksums or version info, leading to incorrect evidence being submitted to a safety case
Incorrect ASIL determination output (wrong table lookup) causes the developer to under-design safety measures for a hazardous item

safetyGoals.description: cfusa shall not suppress or omit any finding for which the rule engine is configured to detect
safetyGoals.safeState: Developer independently reviews code and uses additional static analysis tools

safetyGoals.description: cfusa shall limit its false-positive rate to a level that does not cause systematic check-disabling
safetyGoals.safeState: Developer uses the disposition system to explicitly accept findings with rationale

safetyGoals.description: cfusa impact shall validate all git ref arguments before constructing shell commands
safetyGoals.safeState: validate_git_ref() whitelist prevents injection; the tool exits 1 with an error message

safetyGoals.description: cfusa release/qualify shall compute SHA-256 checksums deterministically and embed the correct project/version from .fusa.json
safetyGoals.safeState: Reviewer independently verifies SBOM checksums against source

safetyGoals.description: cfusa hara asil shall implement ISO 26262-3:2018 Table 4 correctly for all S/E/C combinations
safetyGoals.safeState: Developer cross-checks the ASIL result with ISO 26262-3:2018 Table 4 directly
